root_cause.text: The cleanup path in `memfd_luo_retrieve_folios()` incorrectly passes a raw page frame number (PFN) instead of a physical address to `kho_restore_folio()` and fails to skip sparse file holes where `pfolio->pfn` is zero.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff in `mm/memfd_luo.c` shows that `kho_restore_folio(pfolio->pfn)` was replaced with `kho_restore_folio(PFN_PHYS(pfolio->pfn))` to perform the proper physical address conversion, and a check `if (!pfolio->pfn) continue;` was added to handle sparse file holes.

Author: Pratyush Yadav <pratyush@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Nov 25 11:58:44 2025 -0500

    mm: memfd_luo: allow preserving memfd
    
    The ability to preserve a memfd allows userspace to use KHO and LUO to
    transfer its memory contents to the next kernel.  This is useful in many
    ways.  For one, it can be used with IOMMUFD as the backing store for IOMMU
    page tables.  Preserving IOMMUFD is essential for performing a hypervisor
    live up
bic_trace_step.reason: In the cleanup path of `memfd_luo_retrieve_folios()` (lines 451-458), the code loops through the remaining folios and calls `kho_restore_folio(pfolio->pfn)`. This incorrectly passes the raw PFN (`pfolio->pfn`) instead of the physical address (`PFN_PHYS(pfolio->pfn)`). Additionally, it fails to check `if (!pfolio->pfn) continue;` to skip sparse file holes where the PFN is zero, which is done correctly in the main loop but omitted here.
